nonblocking_observations.finding: Raw double-precision subtraction of nearly equal dynamic and static kernel numerators is unsuitable as a general-purpose small-argument evaluator.
nonblocking_observations.evidence: At real k=1e-4 and r=1e-6 or 1e-8 the direct-double radial/transverse remainder is zero, while 100-digit Cartesian derivative evaluation gives nonzero leading O(k^2/r) terms; observed relative error 1.0.
nonblocking_observations.reason_nonblocking: The supplied raw-double routines are explicitly finite illustrative controls at much larger resolved separations and are not used to certify the continuum limit, analytic ball pole or an effective support index. Their stated replay passes unchanged.
nonblocking_observations.recommendation: If these routines are later reused for small k*r, implement and verify a stable Taylor or expm1-based evaluator before relying on their numerical values.
